blocks.text: The module documentation defines the covered paths, unsafe conditions, limits, and SHA-256 framing. It emphasizes that links are never followed and that the project root location is not included in the digest.
blocks.title: Trust coverage and digest format

blocks.text: Fingerprint carries digest, sorted relative paths, problem code, and total bytes. _Walk holds limits, file hashes, byte totals, and entry counts so partial results remain available when a problem occurs.
blocks.title: Fingerprint and walker state

blocks.anchor: def _open_dir(parent_fd: int, name: str) -> int | None:
blocks.text: Directory traversal uses lstat-style checks and O_NOFOLLOW descriptors. _add_file accepts only regular files, enforces byte and file limits, and hashes content in bounded chunks.
blocks.title: Safe opening and hashing

blocks.anchor: def _walk_dir(self, dir_fd: int, prefix: str, depth: int) -> None:
blocks.text: The walker counts entries and depth, sorts directory names, rejects links and special files, and visits configured files or trees relative to the project root. Its digest frames sorted POSIX paths before file hashes.
blocks.title: Walking selected trees

blocks.text: compute_fingerprint opens the root without following the final path component, visits the fixed trust roots, and turns traversal problems or unexpected errors into a problem-bearing Fingerprint while closing the descriptor.
blocks.title: Bounded fingerprint computation

blocks.text: fingerprint_matches rejects malformed digest strings before computing the folder fingerprint and returns true only for a problem-free exact digest match.
blocks.title: Digest comparison

purpose: The trust decision is tied to bytes in a fixed set of project-controlled configuration trees. The walker opens directories without following links, enforces file, byte, entry, and depth caps, reports the files found so far on problems, and never raises from the public fingerprint operation.
